newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA sees 97 French car mkt down 15.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: PSA sees 97 French car mkt down 15.6 pct.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet revised his market forecast down on Wednesday, telling the annual general meeting he expected French car sales to fall 15.6 percent in 1997 from a year earlier to 1.80 million registrations.
Calvet said the western European car market was expected to increase 2.1 percent this year but with sharply differing performances in the various national markets.

The French market is "crumbling", he said, with year-over- year sales down 23 percent as of June 15. "That has led us to once again revise our forecast which is now 1,800,000 registrations or a drop of 15.6 percent."
Calvet's last forecast issued in May was for a 13 percent fall in French car sales.
Calvet said a price war in France and Europe did not appear to have intensified since the end of 1996.

His growth estimates for the other European car markets are a decline of 0.8 percent for Germany, a rise of 3.7 percent for Britain, an increase of 9.8 percent for Spain and a rise of 26 percent for Italy, thanks to a state rebate programme.
